messages.subject: indexing of multi-dimensional array (3D and beyond)
messages.subject_clean: indexing of multi-dimensional array (3D and beyond)
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I've looked in the documentation and these questions on the Google group about accessing rows and columns in arrays of order 3 and beyond but could not find much on this. Maybe because it is so trivial? :-). As far as I understand arrays of dimension > 2 is not developed in the Eigen library but specifically developed for TMB. I also looked in the matrix_arrays_8cpp-example which has been very useful in many other cases but could not find anything on it there.

Say for example I have a matrix M of dimension I x J, I can access row i by M.row(i).

But what if I have an array A of dimension 3. Say dim of A is I x J x K and I would like  to extract a vector as a function of j given row i and the 3rd dimension k and get a vector as a function of j.

My initial guess was newvector = A.row(i,,k) but that does not seem to work. Have tried several other variations without success.

Kind regards,
Tor

messages.subject_clean: [TMB users] indexing of multi-dimensional array (3D and beyond)
messages.body_plain:
The relevant documentation is

https://kaskr.github.io/adcomp/structarray.html

Due to the memory layout of arrays there's only a column extractor. To get the R equivalent of A[i,,k] one would have to do:

A.col(k).transpose().col(i)

There's some overhead in this construction so it's worth permuting the array if slicing has to be done for many i,j combinations. Use either the 'perm' or 'rotate' method.

messages.subject: random & map in MakeADFun()
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

What happens if I use

MakeADFun(..., random="x",map=list(x=factor(c(1,1,2,2))))

where "x" is a four dimensional parameter vector?

Do we in effect get 2 latent random variables to which the Laplace approximation
is applied?

Does the docs say anything about this?

I have done experiments where I get "convergence", but I have not checked that the likelihood values
are correct.

Hans

messages.subject: Re: random & map in MakeADFun()
messages.body_plain:
Yes, the example will result in two latent variables mapped into the original four variables as x=(x1,x1,x2,x2). The original likelihood contribution of the 4D x-vector no longer integrates to one wrt. (x1,x2).

Haven't really thought about it, but the new function TMB::normalize might be useful in this regard.

My application is a space-time model that I want to reduce to a pure space model (no time effect).

Using "map" I can achieve this with minimal modification of the code. I just include

a flag that removes the spatial prior on “x” except for the first year.
This solves the normalization issue.

messages.subject_clean: Talks focused on TMB at useR! 2018 conference
messages.body_plain:
I am wondering whether anyone is planning to present a TMB related talk at this year's R users conference in Brisbane, Australia, July 10-13? I am thinking of giving a presentation related to constrained optimisation using TMB and the nloptr package, but I don't know of any interesting content not related to my work. I would appreciate any suggestions if you think this is a worthwhile topic to talk about.

https://user2018.r-project.org/

messages.body_plain:
A TMB presentation at useR would be very good. Optimization with "nloptr" in combination of TMB (especially if you provide a TMB-based Jacobian for the constraints)
is powerful, and I think there are a lot of applicaitons for constrained optimization.

I can share some general TMB slides with you if you are interested.
